title: Large line-item total crashes price formatter
reason: Checkpoint assertion failed: "the Line Items form is still on screen with the Name, Quantity and Rate boxes visible"

verdict.title: Large line-item total crashes price formatter
verdict.oneLiner: The Line Items screen crashed instead of showing the requested total of 10000000000000000.00 USD.
verdict.rootCause: The app tries to process a total that is too large for its number formatter, causing a runtime error and replacing the form with an error screen.
verdict.suggestion: Update the total/price formatting path to support this value without converting it to an unsafe JavaScript number, then verify the Line Items form remains visible and shows 10000000000000000.00 USD.

attempts.agentSummary:
I fixed it in `lib/helpers.ts`, but nothing has run yet. A quick script check of the conversion and a type-check both needed approval and didn't run, so the code has only been read through. Gremlin's Kane re-run will decide whether it works.

**Root cause:** Every time the items change, `calculateTotal` in `contexts/ChargesContext.tsx` calls `formatPriceToString`, which passes the integer part of the total to `number-to-words`. That library throws "Input is not a safe number" for anything above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (about 9 quadrillion). A total of 10,000,000,000,000,000 is over that limit, and the uncaught error took down the whole form.

**Change:** I added an `integerToWords` helper that spells big numbers one quadrillion at a time. It passes each chunk small enough for `number-to-words` to the library, so 1e16 becomes "Ten quadrillion". `formatPriceToString` now uses this helper and returns an empty string when the total is NaN or Infinity, instead of throwing.
